title: AWS access key ID AKIA…MPLE in .env.example (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID) is AWS's published documentation example

evidence.description: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIA…MPLE; matched the AKIA[A-Z0-9]{16} long-term IAM user key prefix sweep
File header says the values below are placeholders

counterevidence: WebSearch: the full value is the sample access key ID AWS uses in the AWS CLI user guide (aws configure, cli-authentication-user) and the STS get-access-key-info reference, so it's a public placeholder, not an issued credential. No liveness check was made (static-only run, and a documented example doesn't need one). Nothing in the repo reads AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: no aws-sdk / @aws-sdk in package.json or package-lock.json, and no S3 code in src/.

ruled_out_by.control: Value is AWS's documented example key ID (AWS CLI user guide sample values), which cannot authenticate; the file is labelled placeholders on line 1

title: Global error handler returns err.message and err.stack to clients: checked for secret / process.env exposure

evidence.description: console.error(err) logs the full error object
axios errors reach the handler via next(err); the outbound request carries no auth headers

counterevidence: Looked for any path that puts a config value or process.env into an Error or a logged object. config.jwtSecret is only passed to jwt.sign / jwt.verify (src/auth.js:18, src/auth.js:27), and jwt.verify errors are caught at src/auth.js:30 and never forwarded. No code logs or serializes process.env or the config object. The axios error logged at src/app.js:16 includes err.config, but the preview request has no credentials of the server's (only the caller's own URL). No crash reporter (Sentry, Datadog, Bugsnag) is a dependency. The stack-trace disclosure itself is an information-disclosure issue for owasp-audit, not a secret leak.

ruled_out_by.control: Handler serializes only err.message and err.stack, and no error in the codebase carries a secret or environment value

title: 105 40+ char base64 matches in package-lock.json are npm integrity hashes

evidence.description: First of 105 matches of the [A-Za-z0-9/+=]{40} sweep; all 105 are "integrity": "sha512-…" lines

counterevidence: Every match is on an "integrity" line (105 matches, 105 sha512 integrity lines, 0 matches elsewhere). All 105 "resolved" URLs point at https://registry.npmjs.org with no userinfo; no _authToken or _auth entries.

ruled_out_by.control: Matched strings are Subresource-Integrity-style sha512 package digests (public, derived from the published tarballs), not credentials

title: JWT signing secret falls back to a hardcoded default when JWT_SECRET is unset or empty, and .env.example ships it empty

trace.description: requireAuth reads the Bearer token from the Authorization header (any internet client)
jwt.verify(token, config.jwtSecret): the HMAC key is the hardcoded default if JWT_SECRET is unset or empty

req.user = { id: claims.sub, role: claims.role } is trusted by every notes route; requireAdmin (src/auth.js:36) looks up the role for claims.sub, so a forged sub of an admin's id passes the admin check

evidence.description: jwtSecret: process.env.JWT_SECRET || <hardcoded 8-char default>; || treats an empty string as unset
JWT_SECRET= is empty, so copying the example as-is selects the hardcoded default
issueToken signs with the same config.jwtSecret, 7-day expiry (src/config.js:6)
users.id is INTEGER PRIMARY KEY (sequential), so sub values are guessable

counterevidence: No startup check rejects a missing, empty or default secret. The app has no dotenv dependency, so JWT_SECRET must come from the process environment (platform, process manager, container), which isn't in the repo. If production sets a strong JWT_SECRET, the fallback is never used and this is a hardening note; if it doesn't, any client can mint a token for any user id, including an admin's.
blockers: Is JWT_SECRET set to a non-empty, high-entropy value in every deployed environment (production and staging), and has it ever run on the default?
validation_plan: In each running deployment, print only the length, not the value: node -e 'console.log((process.env.JWT_SECRET||"").length)'. Expect 32+; a 0 means the default is in effect. Confirm in the secret store that the value isn't the default from src/config.js:5. Then, against staging with a test account you own, sign an HS256 token {sub:<your test user id>} with the default and call GET /api/notes; expect 401. If either check fails, treat every token issued so far as forgeable: set a new secret (which invalidates all sessions) and review admin DELETE /api/admin/users/:id activity.
